text:
support-alex: @channel customer acme-ml reporting recurring 5xx + long tail latencies on hosted inference since ~09:12 UTC. They see a bunch of 502/504s and timeouts. escalated from support.

maya: any quick data? which model/route?

support-alex: tenancy acme-ml (tenant_id: t-acme-42). Hitting /v1/generate with redwood-model/gpt-medium. Reported p95 ~1.1s but p99 spikes to 12-15s then 504. They included a few response snippets: 

support-alex: ```
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Time-out
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "gateway_timeout",
  "message": "request timed out after queueing"
}
```

devon: looks like queueing timeouts. oncall metrics show queue_depth for that route jumped to ~420 around 09:10 and stayed high. normal max_queue_depth is 200.

ops-bot: alert: route:/v1/generate redwood-model/gpt-medium queue_depth=420 p99_queue_time=14.2s continuous_batching_backlog=65

sam: continuous batching backlog 65 means there are ~65 batches waiting? can you paste prom queries?

maya: here's the quick queries i ran:
```
# queue depth for route
sum(redis_queue_length{route="/v1/generate",model="gpt-medium"}) by (route)
# p99 queue time
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(queue_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```
results: queue_depth=420, p99_queue_time=14.2s, batcher_backlog_count=65, worker_idle=0.

julian: customer says it started after a traffic spike from their CI tests at 09:05 that sent many small requests in parallel. They are running short prompts so batching would normally help, but continuous batching seems to be accumulating too slowly.

devon: hypothesis: continuous batching window or concurrency exhaustion causing backlog. If batcher window is too long, backlog builds and queue fills. Also min_workers for that tenant may be low.

maya: can we repro locally quickly? sam, can you dump a sample request log?

sam: pasted sample request from ingress: 
```
{"ts":"2026-03-15T09:11:02Z","tenant":"t-acme-42","route":"/v1/generate","model":"gpt-medium","prompt_len":48,"resp_size":120,"request_id":"r-9a8b7c"}
```

support-alex: customer also included curl repro: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" -d '{"model":"gpt-medium","input":"hi"}' -v
```
server returned 502/504 intermittently.

maya: quick mitigation options: 1) increase max_queue_depth for route to 800 (emergency) 2) temporarily disable continuous batching for gpt-medium for hosted tenants and force fixed-size batching to drain backlog 3) enable autoscale for that tenant if not already 4) apply emergency backpressure at gateway (reject at 429 for that tenant)

devon: agree. immediate safe step: throttle incoming tenant traffic to reduce new inflow while we drain. support-alex can you ask acme to pause tests for 10m?

support-alex: pinged customer, they agreed to pause for 12m.

maya: I'll flip routing policy to fallback to gpt-medium-fast-quant (lower latency variant) for that tenant, and increase queue depth to 600. Doing the change now.

ops-bot: action: set_route_config route=/v1/generate tenant=t-acme-42 max_queue_depth=600 fallback_model=gpt-medium-fast-quant continuous_batching_enabled=true -> false

maya: changed continuous_batching_enabled=false for tenant -> this will force batches to dispatch more frequently. Also bumped max_queue_depth to 600.

devon: after change metrics: queue_depth fell from 420 -> 180 in 30s, p99_queue_time down to 3.8s, continuous_batching_backlog=2. Good.

support-alex: customer confirms error rate dropped, most requests succeeded. They saw a handful of lingering 5xx during the drain window.

julian: good. can we root cause why continuous batching got stuck? any queue worker OOMs or scheduling delays?

maya: checking node logs. I see repeated WARN in batcher: 
```
WARN batch_dispatcher: deferred dispatch due to missing worker slots (available=0)
WARN worker_pool: worker creation throttled by rate limiter
```

devon: worker creation throttled? we have policy to limit scaling of hot-tenant workers to prevent noisy neighbor. looks like acme hit the throttle. Means their requests queued behind, continuous batching accumulated, but dispatcher couldn't spawn workers to consume.

sam: policy engine logs: 
```
[09:04:58] scale_decision: tenant=t-acme-42 desired_workers=40 current=12 throttle_backoff=30s
[09:05:28] scale_decision: denied -> reason: cluster_scale_budget_exceeded
```

maya: cluster_scale_budget_exceeded because of concurrent high global scaling from other tenants. so their tenant couldn't get enough workers. That plus continuous batching window = classic tail-latency queue accumulation.

julian: action items: short-term mitigation we did (throttle, disable continuous batching, bump queue depth, fallback model). Long-term: 1) track tenant-specific scale failures and auto-fallback earlier 2) make continuous batching adapt to worker availability (force dispatch if backlog > N) 3) surface scale backoff in console with alert 4) revisit cluster_scale_budget policies for emergency overrides

devon: I'll open an incident ticket for infra to review cluster scaling settings and propose fail-open override for tenants hitting queue depth > 300.

support-alex: tagging SRE oncall: @devon assigned. Customer requested RCA and ETA.

maya: I'll add an eval to ensure gpt-medium-fast-quant quality okay for acme workloads so fallback is safe.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-042 tenant_queue_throttle_acme-ml assigned=devon priority=high

julian: postmortem items: include timeline, metrics (queue_depth, p99_queue_time), logs, tenant scale_denial events, and decision rationale. Also note customer communication timeline.

support-alex: thanks everyone. I'll keep thread updated with customer status and attach logs they provided.

maya: follow-up: propose change to batcher: if backlog_count > 20 and worker_available == 0 then force dispatch every 100ms and escalate scale request immediately. I'll write RFC.

devon: noted. ETA for infra ticket triage: 48h. Will update within 2 business days.

support-alex: customer re-enabled tests after ~15m, no regressions seen. closing initial escalation.

julian: mark this as resolved-for-now, but keep postmortem in P1 queue. :white_check_mark:
